title: __set_name__: descriptors that know their name

kcs.statement: When a class is created, type.__new__ calls __set_name__(self, owner, name) on each class attribute that defines it, passing the attribute's name.
A descriptor should store per-instance values on the instance, for example under a private name derived in __set_name__; storing them on the descriptor itself shares one value across all instances.

problem_ideas: Write a LoggedAccess descriptor that logs 'reading age' using the name from __set_name__
Find the bug where two Person instances share one age value
Predict whether __set_name__ runs for a descriptor added with setattr after class creation
Store values under '_' + name and inspect vars(obj)
Use one descriptor class for both name and age attributes
Predict the owner argument when the descriptor is defined in a base class
